question: The European External Action Service has proposed a special mission to patrol the Red Sea in collaboration with ‘Operation Prosperity Guardian’, set up by the United States. The aim is to monitor the area to ward off the Houthi attacks in Yemen on vessels linked to Israel in response to Israel’s offensive in Gaza, which has already resulted in the deaths of 25 000 Palestinians.

The common foreign and security policy is the framework for this special operation. The aim of that policy is to strengthen international security and foster cooperation. Against the backdrop of the geopolitical tension created by Israel’s genocide in Gaza and the lack of action by Israel’s partners, I would ask the Vice-President / High Representative the following questions: 1.
Does he believe that the EU’s intervention in the Red Sea to protect ships that have economic and trade links to Israel will help to put an end to the genocide?
What consequences will the EU’s military presence in the Red Sea have in the region given that he has still not demanded that Netanyahu put an end to the genocide?
What is his view of the fact that Member States are to take part in the operation without the prior consent of their national parliaments?
answer: Regarding the situation in Gaza, the EU continues to reiterate that the protection of all civilians and unhindered humanitarian access must be ensured by all parties at all times in all conflicts. Full respect of international law including international humanitarian law by all sides is of paramount importance.

The EU has continuously condemned the Houthi attacks against commercial ships and their crews, in grave contravention of international law, threatening maritime security and peace in the region, underlining that they must stop.

In this regard, the High Representative’s declaration on behalf of the EU and its Member States of 12 January 2024 (1), welcomed the 10 January 2024 United Nations Security Council resolution 2722, condemning the Houthi attacks (2).

Operation ‘Prosperity Guardian’ is a multinational military operation led by the United States and launched in December 2023 to respond to Houthi-led attacks on shipping in the Red Sea, of which the EU is not part. On 19 February 2024, the Council launched a new EU maritime operation (Aspides) which will contribute to uphold the freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and beyond.

This operation will aim at protecting merchant vessels, will be defensive in nature and will act in line with the United Nations Security Council Resolution 2272. This initiative is not linked to the situation in Gaza nor Israel’s military operation.
The Member States have their own internal democratic decision-making processes, which will also apply on their individual national decision to participate or not to the new EU maritime operation.
